body: No need for this class, or the class below, I think

It looks like https://github.com/benschwarz/developers.whatwg.org/blob/97ff943a8f5b8fe38f78e224b4b44b472ccefb57/javascript/master.js first found results that started with the phrase, then ones that contained it. Do you think we should keep that?
Maybe factor out this constant (10) into the top of the file

Although the functional style is nice, it does mean we'll iterate over the entire array when we only want 10 elements. It might be better to go with a for loop? Or maybe it doesn't matter. I'm just a little concerned about mobile jank.

A lot of code in https://github.com/benschwarz/developers.whatwg.org/blob/97ff943a8f5b8fe38f78e224b4b44b472ccefb57/javascript/master.js for clearing results and navigating the list seems to be missing.   Should we add it, or do you think it's not necessary?

Not sure if this is related to that but, with the old way it showed some duplicated results:

![](https://imgsthinkxl.s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/esPcd0.png)

This way it fixes the duplicates and show the results in order. 

![](https://imgsthinkxl.s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/ZmiY3Q.png)

(Of course the CSS is missing, I'm working on that)

For me it works better this way, but that doesn't mean that should be the correct way.

What do you think?

I think that for the amount of data we are iterating over (~480 results) we can use `.filter` just fine. Also, in my opinion, this way we can select better results looking into all results.

But I'm probably not thinking through all the constrains, so if a for loop is a better option, lets do it.
Is not necessary, but it's an absolutely nice to have. I'm adding those missing features.
Ah, good catch. I guess let's stick with your way for now as it's simpler and avoids that bug. If it ends up feeling off, we can tweak it later.
Also, we should change the hyphen-minuses (-) to em dashes (—), I guess in the build script.
Happy to stick with the functional style for now and then I can do some measurements to see if it's a real issue.
